'''''Caulerpa sertularioides''''', also known as '''green feather algae''',<ref name=indian>{{cite web|url=http://www.sms.si.edu/irlspec/cauler_sertul.htm|title=''Caulerpa sertularioides'' SG Gmelin Howe, 1905 Green Feather Alga|accessdate=7 November 2018|work=Indian River Lagoon Species Inventory|publisher=[[Smithsonian Institution]]|year=2018}}</ref><ref name=car/> is a species of seaweed in the ''[[Caulerpaceae]]'' family found in warm water environments.<ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Caulerpa sertularioides''|id=26576}}</ref>

==Description==
[[Image:Icones of Japanese algae (Pl. CX) (8006303168).jpg|thumb|left|Three illustrations (Fig 1 . 1-3) of ''C. sertularioides'' displaying its "leaf" and [[rhizome]] structures (Fig 1 . 4-5 are illustrations of [[Caulerpa taxifolia|''C. taxifolia'']])]]
The seaweed has a pale to dark-green [[thallus]] that typically grows to outward to around {{convert|0.35|to|2|m|ft|2}}.<ref name=FloraBase/>  It has feather-like fronds that arise from a common stolon. Each of the fronds is upright and branched. The oppositely arranged branchlets are cylindrical to needle-shaped with upcurved tips with a blunt point at the end. Each branchlet has a length of {{convert|3|to|11|mm|in|3}} and is attached to a cylindrical axis in the middle with a diameter of {{convert|1|to|1.5|mm|in|3|abbr=on}}. Each axis connects each frond to a creeping [[stolon]] with a diameter of {{convert|2|to|2.5|mm|in|3|abbr=on}} and a length of up to {{convert|2|m|ft|0}}. Stolons are branched out to slim points and [[rhizoid]]s then form from bottom surface<ref name=indian/> these fork and penetrate the sandy substrate firmly anchoring the seaweed to the seafloor.<ref name=car>{{cite web|url=http://species-identification.org/species.php?species_group=caribbean_diving_guide&id=490|title=Green feather alga (Caulerpa sertularioides)|work=Interactive Guide to Caribbean Diving |accessdate=7 November 2018|publisher=Marine Species Identification}}</ref>
{{clear|left}}

==Taxonomy==
[[File:Caulerpa sertularioides Munyon Island.jpg|thumb|right|Green Feather Algae (''Caulerpa sertularioides''), A pretty algae species loved by green sea turtles and sea slugs in the shallow waters around [[Munyon Island]].]]
The species was first formally described by the botanist and taxonomist [[Marshall Avery Howe]] in 1905 as part of the work ''Phycological studies - II. New Chlorophyceae, new Rhodophyceae and miscellaneous notes'' as published in the ''Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club''. The [[basionym]] is ''Fucus sertularioides'' as described by [[Samuel Gottlieb Gmelin]] in 1768.<ref name=AB>{{cite web|url=http://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?species_id=1412|title=''Caulerpa sertularioides'' (S.G.Gmelin) M.Howe|accessdate=7 November 2018|work=AlgaeBase|author=Guiry, M.D.|author2=Guiry, G.M.|name-list-style=amp|year=2018|publisher=[[National University of Ireland]], Galway}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is found widely through tropical waters. In the [[United States]] it is found from North Carolina to Florida. It is also found throughout the Caribbean around Bermuda, Bahamas, Greater and Lesser Antilles and in the [[Gulf of Mexico]] and in the southern [[Atlantic Ocean]] to Brazil (Taylor 1979). It is also found in the [[Pacific Ocean]] along the [[Great Barrier Reef]] in Australia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines and Palau.<ref name=indian/> In Western Australia, it is found along the coast in the [[Kimberley (Western Australia)|Kimberley]] region extending south to the [[Gascoyne]].<ref name=FloraBase/>

The species is usually part of coastal and estuarine environments where it grows in sandy areas, as seagrass beds or on and around [[mangrove]] roots. It is mostly found as a shallow-water specimen to depths of around {{convert|10|m|ft|0}} although sparse individuals have been taken from depths of up to {{convert|110|m|ft|0}}.<ref name=indian/>
